sections.title: Habit and identification
sections.text: Greater celandine is a perennial herb 30–100 cm tall, native to Eurasia and naturalised elsewhere. It often grows in hedges, woodland edges and disturbed places. Its blue-green leaves are deeply divided; the yellow flowers have four petals and the linear capsules are about 2–5 cm long.

sections.title: Latex and toxicity
sections.text: A broken stem releases orange-yellow latex. The plant is toxic and its latex can irritate; ingestion or oral medicinal use is not recommended, as liver injury has been associated with some preparations. The plate correctly shows the leaves, flowers, capsules and root.
